column2: 3.1 Currency and completeness

Is there a pre-defined approach to ensure that metadata is kept up-to-date?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe your approach.
column4: The data publishers chooses the frequency of the metadata update, upon the publishing process, which enables the publisher and the user to follow the update schedule.

column2:
What percentage of the metadata on the national portal is obtained from the source automatically, rather than edited manually? 

For Explanation:
* Please describe (1) the workflows you have to automate the harvesting of metadata and (2) for which types of data these apply to
column7: Around 40%, For big data publishers (e.g. Republic Geodata Authority, National Statistics Office, Serbian Environmental Protection Agency...), we create tailor made harvesters.

column2:
What is the average delay from the moment the metadata describing a dataset is updated at the source, and the moment the change is visible on the portal?

For Explanation:
* Please explain the approach for updating metadata in a timely manner
column7: The change is visible within the one day, picked up by harvester.

column2:
Do you undertake efforts to ensure that published data covers the full period from when it was first published until today, for example,the complete time series?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please explain the measures in place to ensure complete series of datasets
column7: Office for IT and eGovernment strongly advices data holders not to replace datasets with new, but instead to keep historical data available. The majority does. The Open Data Portal Editor monitors activities on the Open Data Portal, and keeps open communication with open data publishers, advising them to publish data which covers full periods.

column2: 3.3 DCAT-AP Compliance

Does the national portal follow the DCAT-AP framework or, if not, are standards in place to ensure interoperability with DCAT-AP?

For explanation:
* If the  portal follow the DCAT-AP framework, please describe how compliance with DCAT-AP is ensured
* If the portal does not follow the DCAT-AP framework, please describe how interoperability with DCAT-AP is ensured
column7: Compliance is ensured since the Serbian Open Data Portal uses uData platform developed by the French open data team.  Documentation is in here: https://udata.readthedocs.io/en/stable/rdf/

Do you investigate the most common causes for the lack of DCAT-AP compliance?

column7: The main cause is the fact that many datasets which are not harvested, are entered mannualy, hence the quality depends on the users.

3.4 Deployment quality and linked data

Do you use a model (such as the 5-Star Open Data or FAIR) to assess the quality of deployment of data in your country?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe.
column7: Each dataset comes with a discussion module where users can share their opinions, whether positive or negative. This module also allows users to report any anomalies or suggest areas for improvement to the dataset producer. Consequently, this evaluation system offers more detailed feedback than a simple five-star rating, which fails to provide insights into potential improvements. See example: https://data.gov.rs/sr/datasets/adresni-registar/ uData limits which functions can be added to the Portal, thus for now only qualitative feedback is possible.

column2:
Do you conduct activities to promote and familiarise data providers with ways to ensure higher quality data?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe.
column4: Standards for quality are promoted, especially in cases of highly standardized data (e.g. local expenditure plans). For example, when standard for local budgets was developed, it was sent to all local self-governments in order to use it in case of open data release of their local budget. Also, on trainings, 1 on 1 consultations, open data team always recommends standards recognized in the world, like GTFS for public transport open data, OCDS for public procurement open data, etc. Additionaly, accent is always put on accuracy, consistency, timeliness, completeness and credibility, rather than just quantity.
